Cautiously positive assessment consistent with the literature: Growth remains solid with strong job gains and low unemployment, while inflation has eased but is still above the 2% objective. In line with rule-like behavior estimated by Clarida, Galí, and Gertler and the Fed’s Taylor-rule framework, the FOMC kept the federal funds rate in a restrictive 5.25–5.50% range and continued balance-sheet runoff ($60bn Treasuries, $35bn MBS caps). The insistence on “greater confidence” before cutting aligns with inflation-forecast targeting (Svensson and Woodford) and mitigates time-inconsistency/inflation-bias risks highlighted in the academic literature, complementing the Fed’s average-inflation-targeting shift. Given tight labor markets, New Keynesian Phillips Curve dynamics suggest marginal-cost pressures could keep inflation elevated, justifying vigilance. Maintaining interest on reserve balances at 5.4% and relying on standing repo/reverse repo facilities is consistent with the post-2008 floor system for policy transmission. Net tone: cautiously optimistic on activity, vigilant on inflation, and credibility-focused.
